newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rockets from Lebanon slam into Israel.
newsitem.headline: Rockets from Lebanon slam into Israel.

text.p: Katyusha rockets fired from Lebanon slammed into a northern Israeli town early on Friday, punching holes in a Jewish synagogue and lightly injuring a woman, the army said.

Residents said it was the first time the rockets had landed in Kiryat Shmona, the largest town in Israel's Upper Galilee, in the more than 15 months since Israel and Hizbollah guerrillas undertook not to fire on civilian targets.

A Hizbollah spokesman denied his Iranian-backed Islamic group was behind the attack. But Israeli military sources said they believed it was responsible. They said the rockets had come from the Hizbollah area of Shaqra.
Hizbollah threatened earlier this week to carry out attacks inside Israel. The military sources said the group's denial was prompted apparently by a fear of Israeli retaliation.

Israeli soldiers briefly ordered residents into bomb shelters and security rooms to guard against another possible attack on the town of 22,000 people. Residents later emerged from the rooms and shelters.

Cross-border violence has intensified in recent days. On Thursday five Lebanese were killed. A woman and her two children were killed in the explosion of a roadside bomb planted by unknown assailants.
Also on Thursday, a pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman was killed by a Hizbollah bomb planted in his car and a farmer was killed by retaliatory Israeli shelling.
Five Hizbollah guerrillas were killed early in the week in the explosion of a roadside bomb planted by Israeli commandos.
Avraham Aderi of Kiryat Shmona said he was drinking tea with other residents after morning prayers when the Katyusha slammed into the synagogue. He called it a miracle none of them was hurt.
Hizbollah is fighting to drive the Israelis and their local Lebanese militia allies from Israel's 15-km (nine-mile) occupation zone in south Lebanon.
Israel set up the zone -- a site of frequent rocket attacks, clashes and bombs -- to protect its northern settlements from the Katyushas.

Israel and Hizbollah reached an understanding not to attack civilian targets as part of a 1996 ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught in which about 200 people, mainly Lebanese civilians, were killed.
